headline: Wall Street heads into a week of big company results with investors nervous that the AI-led stock rally is losing steam.
score_reason: Reuters preview of the earnings test for AI spending after a rough week; forward-looking, so it carries less weight than the sell-off itself.
importance_line: Holders of index funds and of Meta, chip makers and Tesla are affected first, then suppliers that depend on AI spending, though strong results may not calm worries about debt and higher interest rates, which Reuters says also remain on investors' minds.
summary: Reuters reports that Wall Street enters a week of company results, led by Meta, Tesla, SpaceX, Lam Research and Texas Instruments, after AI-linked chip and hardware shares fell this week and left investors nervous about the rally. Goldman Sachs expects five giant AI cloud companies, Meta among them, to raise their combined capital spending to about $1.2 trillion next year, and Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth, says the key question is whether their profits can grow faster than that spending.
notes: Reuters Week Ahead column read on the Devdiscourse syndicated copy; reuters.com link kept as the original.
